source.title: Intraday lottery demands in cryptocurrency market

hypothesis: Cryptocurrencies with extreme positive intraday returns attract lottery-like demand and subsequently underperform; a daily long-low-MAX / short-high-MAX portfolio should earn positive net returns.
universe: Frozen ex-ante Binance USD-M USDT perpetuals listed by 2021-12-31, including later-delisted contracts where data exist. At each UTC day open retain top 50 by lagged trailing-30-day quote volume.
feature: Negative maximum completed hourly close-to-close return over the prior H hours, measured before the 00:00 UTC rebalance. Higher signal means lower lottery-like MAX exposure.
portfolio: Equal-weight market-neutral long highest -MAX quintile / short lowest -MAX quintile, 0.5 gross each side.
execution: Signal and liquidity inputs end at 23:00 UTC of the prior day; execute at current 00:00 UTC open and hold to next 00:00 UTC open.
development_gate: Canonical mean daily rank IC >0.02 with HAC p<0.05, positive high-minus-low signal spread, canonical net Sharpe >0.70 and total return >0, and at least 2/3 lookbacks positive after costs.
success_gate: Canonical OOS net Sharpe >1.0; OOS rank IC >0.02; positive at 2x costs; at least 2/3 lookbacks positive; 2024 and 2025 non-negative; max drawdown <35%; excluding BTC/ETH positive; excluding strongest contributor positive; DSR reported.
notes: The source studies intraday MAX/lottery demand. Hourly Binance perpetual bars are the finest common panel used here, so the test measures hourly rather than trade-level intraday extremes.
